WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 1 of provider_network_services (Vaughn Dental Arts PLLC, Cascade PPO Participating Dentist Agreement, weekly claim runs). Revision 2 (rework round 2).

STEP 0 DRAW (draw_counts.py --task 1): {"task": 1, "key": "env_0070_dental_and_vision_benefits_carrier/provider_network_services/1", "prerequisite_problems": 3, "problems": 4, "factor_counts": [6, 6, 6, 6]}. Four computations of 6 factors; 3 prerequisite problems, all three edges value_input (>= 2).

REVISION LOG (round 2): S1 — the staff list-bill billing account (forbidden by the billing entry gate for a provider_practice profile) was removed; the cross-category evidence is now the practice's own Cascade employer group contract in status applied with its census report (group.yaml carries no customer_type gate; an applied contract needs no billing account, enrolment or premium yet); the plan premium-standing factor became the plan small-practice addition (staff headcount on the latest census) and the down payment premium-standing factor became a dispute-history factor on provider records. S2 — every notice is now an overpayment of a re-issued claim payment run that is on the ledger with the same amount (OVP75-2604-0583 <- re-issue of the 2026-03-13 run, OVP75-2609-0714 <- 2026-08-21, OVP75-2609-0738 <- 2026-08-28, OVP75-2610-0802 <- 2026-09-25), source_product not_applicable because they arose from remittances, not member claims; the two 2025 notices without supporting records were removed. C3a/C3b — the run policy now computes its claim-paid scope (capitation agreements excluded), the post-decision policy computes 'first withholding only' and 'not before the day after the decision'. C4+C5 — one shared scoped replacement of the base offset-order and practice-level sentences names the selections of the continuing, post-decision and plan withholdings, and the plan installment also replaces the refund-window start sentence for itself only, so the installment's object follows uniquely from in-force sentences. C6 — the down payment is capped at the open amount of the overpayment it is recorded against. C7 — the installment scope sentence and both tool docstrings no longer restate the down-payment dependency. C8b/C8c — prompt-dispute tiers 10/20 days and notice-age tiers 50/75 days leave reachable fall-throughs (filings of 21-30 days; notices 46-50 days old at the run). C9 — combination sentences no longer name factor quantities. C10 — the plan balance measure's tiers now differ in shape (less one overpayment's open amount; less the lesser of an open amount and the run's standard room; whole receivable). The run aging fall-through moved to 10 days or fewer, which a weekly continuing withholding can reach (8-10 days).

REVISION LOG (round 3): N5 — the continuing run withholding is now owed at most once per claim payment run and only as the run's first entry, and the first plan installment is stated to be the run's last entry, so the order between them is fixed by in-force sentences: re-evaluated after the down payment the continuing withholding is 0.00, after the installment 0.00, and a second installment on the same run is 0.00. N2 — the plan small-practice addition no longer turns on buying staff coverage (the round 3 payments measure is removed in round 4, see below). N1/N3 — coordinator ruling, unchanged.

REVISION LOG (round 4): R3-N2 — the payments proxy is removed. The plan small-practice addition requires a documented employee headcount; the only headcount documentation Cascade holds for a practice is the census on the practice's own Cascade staff group contract, so the addition reads the latest census of that contract while it has not ended (applied or active), and a practice with no census on file, an ended contract or a larger documented headcount is on the standard terms (a stated tier, +0 runs); the rule makes no same-size claim. Here the contract is applied and its latest census documents 3 employees, so the addition is unchanged. O10 — closed with the proxy.

REVISION LOG (round 5): R4-N7 (replaces the round 4 handling of R3-N6) — the claim payment marker is removed: book_plan_installment_e88126b0 books its entry with remittance component not_applicable, as the schema requires for overpayment entries, so an installment entry looks like every other withholding entry. The plan once-per-run sentence now states the base limit of one withholding entry per overpayment per remittance, and rule and compute alike block the installment when the run already carries any withholding entry for the overpayment the plan down payment was recorded against. In this world the installment run's two earlier entries are on other overpayments, so the installment is unchanged.

WHY IT IS A GOOD TEST: the caller asks only to set up a payment plan and start it today. The first installment waits on the down payment, the down payment on the post-decision withholding, and that on the continuing withholding of the older overpayment under recovery — each a six-factor computation consuming the previous write, the run, notices, refunds, decisions and (through the plan small-practice addition) the census of the practice's own Cascade group contract.

SCOPE SNAPSHOT: task 0 owns repayment interest, capitation continuation and exit settlement; this task owns provider_ext_run_continuation (book_run_withholding_d2ce9ec8), provider_ext_decision_resumption (book_decision_withholding_431b56e1), provider_ext_plan_down_payment (pay_plan_down_payment_331c146f), provider_ext_plan_installment (book_plan_installment_e88126b0). Disjoint; together all seven.

POLICIES AND OVERWRITES: run continuation and decision resumption (state_due) and the plan installment (on_request) each carry the two scoped overwrites of provider_agg_practice_offset (practice-level reach; offset order and limits), with the identical replacement sentences shared by the capitation continuation, each naming all four selecting withholdings; the plan installment adds scoped overwrites of the refund-window sentence and of 'The offset may start on the day after the notice date plus overpayment_refund_window_days calendar days.'. The down payment (on_request) has overwrite [].

user_scenario:
You are Trina Ulrich, the practice administrator at Vaughn Dental Arts PLLC in Spokane, calling Cascade Mutual's provider line for Dr. Simone Vaughn. You are friendly and talkative but a bit worried about cash flow. The practice has had several overpayment notices from Cascade this year, most of them about payments that reached the practice twice after it changed banks, and money has been kept back from its weekly payments; Dr. Vaughn would rather the practice paid what it owes in steady, predictable amounts. You open by saying that, and you ask to set up a payment plan for what the practice owes Cascade on its PPO agreement and to get the plan started today. You are authorised to agree to the plan for the practice. You do not know how Cascade sizes a plan or what it would cost each week, and you do not suggest numbers.

You give details only when the representative asks for them. If asked how to find the practice, you give the Cascade provider number PN75-62094. To confirm who you are, you give the practice phone number 4255550177 and, if a second detail is needed, the last four digits of the practice tax ID, 5872. If asked which agreement, it is the Cascade PPO participating dentist agreement for Dr. Simone Vaughn, the only agreement the practice has. If asked about the notices, you recall that the practice disputed one of them in September and heard recently that the dispute did not go its way, and that the newest notice arrived in October; the representative can see the details. If asked whether the practice deals with Cascade in any other way, you say it applied in October for a Cascade dental plan for its three employees, to start in December. You cannot answer questions about Cascade's internal processes.

If the representative explains that something has to happen before the plan can start, you say that makes sense and to go ahead. If the representative says the practice has to pay something itself to start the plan, you say the practice can pay it today from its operating account by electronic payment, and when the representative hands you the payment step you make the payment for exactly the amount and the overpayment reference you are given and read back the confirmation. When the representative tells you the plan has started and what has been kept back from today's payment for it, you thank them and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: The tree is a chain: each problem's prerequisite sentence pins its single predecessor (the post-decision withholding waits on the continuing withholding of the older overpayment, the down payment on the post-decision withholding, the first installment on the down payment). The continuing run withholding is the run's first entry and is owed at most once per run, and the first plan installment is the run's last entry, so no second continuing withholding competes with the installment: re-evaluated after the down payment the continuing withholding is 0.00, after the installment 0.00, and the installment re-evaluated after its own booking is 0.00.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Without the down payment the first installment becomes 73.06 instead of 36.40, and the refund entry is missing.
Without the post-decision withholding the down payment becomes 971.37 instead of 953.02.
Without the continuing withholding the post-decision withholding becomes 793.78 instead of 129.22.
